complexity.correctness_reason: Arrival times are compared as floats, and within NeetCode's caps (values <= 1e6) distinct fractions are always distinguishable in double precision, but with uncapped magnitudes two distinct times like 10^18/1 and (10^36-1)/10^18 round to the same double and the comparison goes the wrong way — exact integer cross-multiplication of (target-pos)*speed would stay correct at any magnitude.
complexity.notes: Swapping the comparison sort for a position-indexed array drops the ordering step to O(target), which under the given scaling (target ~ 2n) makes the whole solution linear. The `cars.pop()` / `cars[-1]` stack walk from the previous version is unchanged. No asymptotic improvement is available for the ordering step itself since positions arrive unsorted; the remaining work is already a single linear pass.
complexity.summary: Places each car into a position-indexed array of length target (a counting sort), compacts it, then pops from the destination end, comparing each car's arrival time to the current fleet leader's and counting a new fleet whenever a car arrives strictly later.
